text:
Maria: Hey team — customer seeing repeated 401 invalid_api_key errors for embeddings after a key rotation. They say the same request works for another teammate. Posting the repro they gave.

Ian (Support): Got it. Can you paste the curl you used (masking secrets ok) and the exact response body / headers? Also which environment (hosted vs dedicated) are they calling?

Maria: Here is the curl they ran (sanitized):
```
curl -v \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer redwood-service-01" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```
Response: HTTP/1.1 401
{"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"Invalid API key."}

Ian (Support): Thanks. Two quick checks: 1) Is that value the full secret (starts with something like "redwood_") or is it an ID string? 2) Are they hitting the hosted api.redwood.ai endpoint (vs a dedicated/private hostname)?

Kayla: They said they copied the value from our Vault output. This is what the ops engineer ran:
```
$ vault kv get secret/redwood/service
Key     Value
----    -----
id      redwood-service-01
secret  redwood_abcXYZ==
```
I think they copied the `id` field earlier. Oops.

Alex (SRE): Confirming from our request logs: incoming request had Authorization header "Bearer redwood-service-01" and we attempted lookup by ID but no active secret matched that token -> 401. The correct secret string is the `secret` value (redwood_abcXYZ==). This is a pretty common slip when Vault shows both id/secret. Also note: dedicated keys are bound to a different hostname; if they mistakenly use a dedicated key against hosted endpoint you can also get 401. Logs show this one was a plain ID mismatch though.

Ian (Support): Steps to remediate:
1) From Vault or Dashboard, copy the `secret` (value that begins with `redwood_`).
2) Re-run the curl with the secret in the Authorization header: 
```
curl -v \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer redwood_abcXYZ==" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```
3) If still 401, verify the key scope/org: `GET https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys/me` (will return masked metadata) or check Dashboard -> API keys for which environment (hosted/dedicated) the key is valid for.

Ian (Support): Also a note for ops: when sharing repro steps internally, call out which Vault field is the secret (we've added a quick doc blurb on this). For CI systems prefer storing the secret value in a named env var, not the ID.

Kayla: Tried the secret value — success, embeddings returned 200 and tokens. Thanks! :tada:

Maria: Customer confirmed fixed after we pointed them at the secret field. Closing the escalation but leaving a note: ops learning: don't confuse key ID with secret when teaching SRE/Dev on rotation flows.

deploy-bot: Logged event: key-rotation-confirmation for org:acme-corp user:kayla at 2024-05-21T14:05:00Z

Alex (SRE): I'll add a one-liner to our vault docs to emphasize "copy the secret value (secret) not the id" and a quick CI snippet for safe env var usage.

Ian (Support): Great. Marking thread resolved. If they hit a dedicated vs hosted mismatch, reopen and include the failing request_id and target hostname. :thumbsup:
